title: Fancy print()
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to print several values on one line and how to make a blank line.
learn: Give print() several values separated by commas
Python puts a space between those values for you
An empty print() makes a blank line
idea: You can give print() several things separated by commas, and Python puts a space between them automatically. You do not have to type the spaces yourself. An empty print() with nothing inside the parentheses prints a blank line, which is useful for spacing out your output so it is easier to read.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change 10 to 25 in the first print and press Run. The first line should say Score: 25 points.

practice.text: Finish the mini scoreboard. Each player should print on one line like Alice: 42 points. Fill in the blank print.
practice.hint: Copy the pattern from the Alice line: a name in quotes, a number, and the word points, all inside one print() with commas between them.
practice.starterTip: Fill the blank print like: print("Bob:", 30, "points"). Change the name and number to your second player.
practice.starter:
print("Alice:", 42, "points")
# Player 2. Finish this line
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if there are two print lines that each show a player name, a number, and the word points (commas between values is fine). Empty print() fails.

practice.text: Print a title, then a blank line, then a message. Use one empty print() for the blank line.
practice.hint: The title and the empty print() for spacing are already there. Only the last print() needs text inside quotes.
practice.starterTip: Leave print("NEWS") and print() as they are. Fill the bottom blank with something like print("Breaking story here").
practice.starter:
print("NEWS")
# Blank line
print()
# Message after the blank line
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if output has a title print, one empty print() for a blank line, and another print with non-empty text after it.

quiz.question: What does print("Hi", "Sam") show?
quiz.correct: Right, commas in print() put a space between the values.
quiz.wrong: print() inserts a space between each value. It does not add a comma.

quiz.question: What does an empty print() do?
quiz.correct: Yes, an empty print() makes a blank line.
quiz.wrong: An empty print() does not cause an error. It just prints a blank line.

quiz.question: How many values can you pass to one print()?
quiz.correct: Right, you can list as many values as you want, separated by commas.
quiz.wrong: One print() can take lots of values as long as they are separated by commas.
